chapter: Ellington colleagues, singers and world tours
title: Alice Babs
summary: He first heard her in Scandinavia and discusses her Sacred Concert trip in 1968.

venues.name: Cathedral of St. John the Divine

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: I -- when you mentioned the Scandinavian countries, I am reminded of another singer that Alice Baks you didn't mention (unintelligible).

Alice, yeah, she came over here a couple of times in some of the concerts. She is very unique. She has a terrific voice. She handles it very well. She's a nice person, very nice, and I would say that she is one of the biggies in her work.
Did you first hear her in Europe, in Scandinavia?
I did. First time I heard her was in Scandinavia.
Didn't she make a recording with the Ellington band that was released only in Europe?

I'm not sure of that. I think she did make a recording of something, but I don't know what it was. Or I don't remember where it was. See, these things happen, as I say, so quickly and so -- it's distributed -- that you can't keep track of them too well.
And then she came (unintelligible). to New York in 1968 to sing in the Second Sacred Concert at the Cathedral of St. John the Divine.
And then she stayed for a week and sang at subsequent concerts in New England and then recorded for a concert tour over there?
Oh, yes. Yes, I heard that, uh-huh.
Well, you were in the band then in 1968.
